svg.text: Maritime Cyber Risk — IT and OT on Board

g.text: IT — information systems
Business email, crew internet, planned
maintenance, cargo and stores software,
administrative networks.
If it fails
Data is lost or stolen. Costly and
disruptive, but the ship still steers.
Usually the way in for an attacker.
OT — operational technology
ECDIS, GNSS, AIS, radar, VDR, engine and
power management, ballast and cargo
control, steering.
If it fails
The ship itself is affected — navigation,
propulsion or stability.
This is why the two must stay separated.
How it usually gets in
Phishing email to a crew or office account
USB stick brought on board — chart updates,
service engineer's laptop
Unpatched software left at an old version
Shared or default passwords never changed
Remote access left open for a supplier
What is required
Cyber risk is managed inside the existing
safety management system (IMO 2021).
Identify · Protect · Detect · Respond · Recover
Segregate OT from IT; control removable media;
unique accounts; keep offline backups of charts
and settings; drill the fallback to paper and
manual steering, because that is the real defence.
